pulls.title: 8394082: RISC-V: Remove redundant membar from C1 compareAndSet
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, please consider. In C1, do_CompareAndSwap and do_UnsafeGetAndSet resolve through LIRGenerator::access_atomic_cmpxchg_at / access_atomic_xchg_at, which default to the MO_SEQ_CST decorator. So casw/caswu/casl (cas_int/uint/long) and atomic_op (lir_xadd/lir_xchg) all require MO_SEQ_CST. On RISC-V, MacroAssembler::cmpxchg is already emitted with acquire (on the load) and release (on the store), and the atomic_op path uses atomic_addal/atomic_xchgal, i.e. amoadd.aqrl / amoswap.aqrl. Each of these is then followed by an unconditional membar(AnyAny) (fence rw,rw). This change removes that trailin

pulls.title: 8307970: Thread.start is slow with large number of threads
pulls.author: fbredber
pulls.body_excerpt: This PR reduces the Thread-SMR (Safe Memory Reclamation) related cost of starting and exiting threads. Both starting and exiting a thread create a new `ThreadsList` and retire the old one. Previously, we used to scan the hazard pointers of all threads when a `ThreadsList` was retired. This made the execution cost increasingly higher as more threads were started. This PR tackles the problem in three ways: 1. By not scanning hazard pointers every time a new thread is started. Instead, we defer the scanning until either 16 `ThreadsLists` have been retired or the retired lists occupy at least 4 MB

pulls.body_excerpt: ### Summary: The goal of this PR is to eliminate the following race-prone pattern in CDS archive mapping code on Windows: - Reserve a large range. - Release the entire range. - Quickly map archive file sections into subregions within the original range. The reason this pattern exists is because Windows previously did not allow mapping into reserved regions. It also did not allow splitting up a reserved region. pulls.title: 8392333: RISC-V: Use RVV to improve indexof intrinsic
pulls.author: kuaiwei
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, this patch implements simd stubs for `String::indexOf` methods. Currently implements scheme described in http://0x80.pl/articles/simd-strfind.html The general idea is as follows: 1. Broadcast the first char of the needle to a first-char vector register 2. Broadcast the last char of the needle to a last-char vector register 3. Compare the first-char vector register to the first position of the haystack 4. Compare the last-char vector register to the (k-1)st position of the haystack where k is the length of the needle 5. Logically AND the results of the comparison to find candidates of match

pulls.title: 8391921: RISC-V: Add C2 vector support for CompressBitsV and ExpandBitsV
pulls.author: zifeihan
pulls.body_excerpt: Hi, This PR adds RISC-V RVV support for the C2 CompressBitsV and ExpandBitsV nodes for int and long element types. These nodes are generated by Vector API operations such as VectorOperators.COMPRESS_BITS and VectorOperators.EXPAND_BITS, and may also be generated by SuperWord for suitable scalar loops. This is different from the scalar CompressBits/ExpandBits implementation removed by JDK-8334474. The old implementation used RVV instructions to process one scalar value at a time. This change operates on multiple vector lanes in parallel. ### Performance test JMH test case: https://bugs.openjdk.

pulls.title: 8389111: C2: Use BMI2 BZHI for variable int low-bit masks on x86
pulls.author: aprilivy
pulls.body_excerpt: C2 currently lowers variable `int` low-bit masks of the form: value & ((1 << bits) - 1) to a five-instruction sequence on x86. This change adds a BMI2 matcher rule that uses `BZHI`, reducing it to three instructions. The shift count is explicitly masked with `31` because Java shift distances wrap modulo 32, while `BZHI` treats counts greater than or equal to 32 differently. A scalar JMH throughput benchmark on a Ryzen 9 9950X3D improved from approximately 0.199 ns/op to 0.185 ns/op (6.9%). pulls.title: 8387392: Windows AArch64: compiler/escapeAnalysis/TestBCEscapeAnalyzerOverflow.java fails
pulls.author: swesonga
pulls.body_excerpt: When the AArch64 template interpreter generates fixed frames, it makes enough room on the stack for the maximum number of entries on the expression stack (max_stack) by subtracting this value from the stack pointer (when max_stack is 0xFFFF, this is about 512KB). This is problematic on Windows because it lets subsequent code access pages deeper in the stack without any of these intermediate stack pages having been accessed.
